title: Emirate of Sicily
capsule: The Emirate of Sicily emerged from the Aghlabid conquest begun in 827 CE, when forces from Ifriqiya landed at Mazara del Vallo; Palermo fell in 831 and became the Muslim capital under the name al-Madinah, and Syracuse was taken in 878. Under the Kalbid emirs, who governed from 948 as autonomous vassals of the Fatimid Caliphate, Sicily reached its administrative and cultural peak, supporting a mixed Arab-Berber-Greek population and an economy linked to the broader Islamic Mediterranean. Kalbid authority collapsed in internal strife after 1044, fragmenting the island into competing taifas. Norman forces under Roger de Hauteville systematically captured the divided fiefdoms; Palermo fell in 1072, and the last Muslim strongholds at Noto and Butera surrendered in 1091, ending over two and a half centuries of Islamic rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The broad chronology is well documented in Arab and Norman sources, but the interior boundaries of Muslim-controlled territory during the taifa fragmentation period (1044–1091) are uncertain.
